translationEn:
To all employees,
Information Systems Department

Starting on the 1st of next month, we will sequentially replace PCs that are over four years old with new models. Eligible staff will be notified of their exchange date via individual email by this Friday.

By the day before your exchange, please be sure to save all necessary files on your desktop to the company cloud. Once the old PC is returned, data cannot be recovered. Please note that email history and internal chat data transfer automatically, so backing them up is unnecessary.

questions.explanationEn: Only PCs 4+ years old are replaced sequentially, and eligible staff receive an individual email by this Friday.

items.titleJp: 工場[こうじょう]見学[けんがく]の日程[にってい]変更[へんこう]のご相談[そうだん]

translationEn:
Dear Public Relations Representative, Aoba Foods Co., Ltd.,
Thank you always for your kind support. My name is Sasaki from Sakura University.

I am writing regarding the factory tour we reserved for Tuesday the 12th of next month at 10:00 AM. Due to a sudden class schedule change, more than half of the 25 planned students can no longer attend in the morning.

I am terribly sorry for the selfish request, but would it be possible to move it to 2:00 PM on the same day, or to 10:00 AM on Thursday the 14th? If neither is possible, we will visit as originally scheduled with only the students who can attend. Thank you for checking.

items.titleJp: 「ながらスマホ」が奪[うば]う記憶[きおく]
items.titleEn: Memories Stolen by Distracted Phone Use
items.contextEn: Short column discussing attention and memory in everyday life.
paragraphs: 映画[えいが]を見[み]ながら、あるいは家族[かぞく]と食卓[しょくたく]を囲[かこ]みながら、ついスマートフォンを触[さわ]ってしまうことはないだろうか。ちょっとした通知[つうち]を確認[かくにん]するだけのつもりでも、意識[いしき]が一度[いちど]途切[とぎ]れると、元[もと]の会話[かいわ]や映像[えいぞう]に集中[しゅうちゅう]し直[なお]すのに思[おも]った以上[いじょう]の時間[じかん]がかかる。
ある心理学[しんりがく]の調査[ちょうさ]では、スマホを机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に置[お]いておくだけで、見[み]ていなくても人[ひと]の注意[ちゅうい]力[りょく]が下[さ]がるという結果[けっか]が出[で]ている。楽[たの]しい時間[じかん]をしっかり記憶[きおく]に残[のこ]すためには、通知[つうち]を切[き]ってカバンの中[なか]にしまっておく工夫[くふう]が効果[こうか]的[てき]だ。
translationEn: Have you ever found yourself reaching for your smartphone while watching a movie or sharing a meal with family? Even if you only intend to check a quick notification, once your attention breaks, it takes longer than expected to refocus on the conversation or film.

In one psychology study, results showed that simply leaving a smartphone on the desk reduces attention even without looking at it. To preserve enjoyable moments vividly in memory, turning off notifications and keeping the phone tucked inside a bag is an effective habit.

questions.explanationEn: Paragraph 2 says merely placing a smartphone on the desk lowers attention even without looking at it.

questions.explanationEn: The closing sentence recommends turning off notifications and putting the phone away inside a bag.

items.titleJp: 「失敗[しっぱい]ノート」をつける意味[いみ]
items.titleEn: The Value of Keeping a "Mistake Notebook"
items.contextEn: Essay about learning effectively from errors in language study and work.
paragraphs: 試験[しけん]の練習[れんしゅう]問題[もんだい]を解[と]いたあと、点数[てんすう]だけを見[み]て「よかった」「だめだった」で終[お]わらせてしまう人[ひと]は少[すく]なくない。しかし、本当[ほんとう]に実力[じつりょく]が伸[の]びるのは、間違[まちが]えた問題[もんだい]に向[む]き合[あ]う瞬間[しゅんかん]だ。
私[わたし]は語学[ごがく]の勉強[べんきょう]をするとき、間違[まちが]えた単語[たんご]や文法[ぶんぽう]だけをまとめた「失敗[しっぱい]ノート」を作[つく]っている。大事[だいじ]なのは正解[せいかい]を写[うつ]すことではなく、「なぜその選択肢[せんたくし]を選[えら]んでしまったのか」という自分[じぶん]の勘違[かんちが]いを一行[いちぎょう]書[か]き添[そ]えることだ。
そうやって見返[みかえ]してみると、自分[じぶん]に共通[きょうつう]する弱点[じゃくてん]のパターンが見[み]えてくる。失敗[しっぱい]を隠[かく]すのではなく記録[きろく]して活[い]かすことこそが、遠回[とおまわ]りに見[み]えて一番[いちばん]の近道[ちかみち]なのである。
translationEn: After solving practice exam questions, quite a few people just look at their score, think "great" or "no good," and stop there. However, true ability grows in the moment you confront the questions you got wrong.

When I study languages, I make a "mistake notebook" gathering only the words and grammar I missed. What matters is not copying down the correct answer, but jotting down one line about my own misunderstanding: "Why did I choose that option?"
When you review it that way, common patterns in your weaknesses emerge. Rather than hiding mistakes, recording and leveraging them may look like a detour, yet it is actually the fastest shortcut.

練習[れんしゅう]問題[もんだい]はたくさん解[と]くほど点数[てんすう]が自動[じどう]で上[あ]がる。
語学[ごがく]の勉強[べんきょう]では、ノートを作[つく]ると遠回[とおまわ]りになる。

items.titleJp: キャッシュレス決済[けっさい]と現金[げんきん]払い[ばらい]（A/B比較[ひかく]）
items.titleEn: Cashless Payment vs. Paying with Cash (A/B Comparison)
items.contextEn: Two consumers compare cashless mobile payments and traditional cash.
items.labelA: Aさんの意見[いけん]（キャッシュレス派[は]）
items.labelB: Bさんの意見[いけん]（現金[げんきん]派[は]）
paragraphs: 私[わたし]は買[か]い物[もの]のほとんどをスマートフォンやカードで支払[しはら]っている。レジで小銭[こぜに]を探[さが]す手間[てま]がなく、会計[かいけい]が一瞬[いっしゅん]で終[お]わるのが快適[かいてき]だ。
さらに、アプリを見[み]れば「いつ・どこで・いくら使[つか]ったか」が自動[じどう]で記録[きろく]されるため、家計[かけい]簿[ぼ]をつける必要[ひつよう]がない。ポイントも貯[た]まるので、結果[けっか]的[てき]に節約[せつやく]にもつながっている。
paragraphsB: キャッシュレス決済[けっさい]が便利[べんり]なのは認[みと]めるが、私[わたし]はあえて現金[げんきん]を中心[ちゅうしん]に使[つか]っている。スマホでピッと払[はら]うだけだと「お金[かね]が減[へ]った」という実感[じっかん]が薄[うす]く、つい予定[よてい]以上[いじょう]に買[か]いすぎてしまうからだ。

translationEn: I pay for most of my shopping using a smartphone or card. There is no hassle looking for coins at the register, and checkout finishes in an instant, which feels great.

Moreover, checking the app shows an automatic record of when, where, and how much I spent, so there is no need to keep a manual budget book. Reward points also accumulate, leading to savings as a result.

With cash, you can visually see the remaining balance in your wallet and prevent wasteful spending. There is also peace of mind knowing you can definitely pay even during power outages or network disruptions.
